title: tune NCCL streams and scheduling to improve comm/compute overlap in tensor-parallel collectives
author: Miguel Alvarez
description: Motivation: In multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) setups we observed suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and CUDA kernels when continuous batching and KV cache are active. This PR tunes NCCL stream usage, introduces a lightweight scheduling heuristic, and pins collective ordering to improve comm/compute overlap with minimal behavioral changes. Summary of changes: 1) Add per-TensorParallelRank dedicated NCCL comm streams and prioritized stream scheduling so asynchronous collectives can run without blocking compute kernels. 2) Introduce 'tp_comm_stream_priority' runtime config (default: enabled) and a heuristic that prefers launching small collectives on a lower-priority comm stream to reduce interference with critical kernels. 3) Adjust ordering of all-reduce/all-gather ops in the TP graph to favor overlap-friendly ordering and add explicit stream synchronization only where necessary (instead of global device syncs). 4) Add a fallback path for drivers without stream priority support to preserve previous behavior. 5) Update the TP comm manager (comm_manager.cc) and the Python scheduler interface (runtime/tp/scheduler.py) to expose the new controls and to log per-request scheduling decisions for perf debugging. 6) Tests and docs: microbench harness (tests/tp/test_nccl_overlap.py) and a perf note documenting tuning knobs (docs/perf/nccl_tuning.md). Notes: - This is a focused runtime change; it does not change model kernels or the topology abstraction. - Default behavior preserves compatibility; enabling the heuristic is safe for typical enterprise GPUs but can be toggled per-deployment. Checklist: - [x] microbench results on A100/H100 clusters - [x] unit tests for scheduling fallback - [x] integration test across 8xA100 with continuous batching - [x] docs updated with tuning guidance

review_comments: Jordan Kim: Please add a guard for driver versions that don't support stream priority; we saw CI failures on an older CI image.
Miguel Alvarez: Added fallback to default stream for drivers without priority and added a unit test that simulates no-priority devices.
Lena Schmidt: Nice work. Microbench numbers look promising; please add a short release note.
release_notes: Improved NCCL comm/compute overlap for tensor-parallel workloads by introducing prioritized comm streams and a scheduling heuristic. Default behavior is backwards compatible. See docs/perf/nccl_tuning.md for guidance.
performance_results: 8xA100 seq_len=2048 bs=8 continuous batching: tail P95 latency reduced 12%
4xH100 seq_len=4096: tail latency reduced 9% and throughput +4%
Fallback path preserves previous performance on older drivers (no-change)
notes: This change improves production TP latency and throughput in our hosted clusters. Ops teams were consulted to roll out the default enabled flag for recent driver images only. We recommend enabling the heuristic on Dedicated clusters running driver >= 470.XX for best results.
